supporters.quote: No significant correlation was found between depression severity measured by K-GDS and ROI volumes in any of the four groups. [...] We have not found any significant correlation between depression severity measured by K-GDS and resting-state FC in any of the four groups. / (Abstract) MDD groups had lower FC than STD groups in the frontal, cortical, and limbic areas.
supporters.note: Hyung et al. 2021, J Affect Disord; Korea University Guro; 43 controls plus 87 late-life-depression MCI patients (N = 130); VBM, resting-state FC and florbetaben PET; cross-sectional. Supports the row's severity clause and its 'although' clause. Limits: every patient is both depressed and MCI (no non-depressed MCI group), so the paper cannot test the first clause (depression status associated with MCI); subgroups of 14 to 28 with Bonferroni thresholds of 0.002 to 0.006 make the null correlations low-powered; a planned voxel-wise BDI correlation within MDD is described in the methods but no result is reported. The authors themselves read categorical severity as grading the brain ('Subjects with more severe depression had greater gray matter loss and altered brain connectivity', p. 6), which fits the row's 'divided' framing. The ledger note overstates one point: the STD-MCI-A(+) group showed greater FC reduction than the MDD-MCI-A(-) and STD-MCI-A(-) groups (abstract, p. 1), not than the MDD-MCI-A(+) group.

supporters.quote: The results of Cox regression analysis showed that only baseline MoCA scores could predict the risk of future MCI transition to dementia (p < 0.001, HR = 0.738, 95 % confidence interval: 0.627–0.869). / (Table 4) GDS 5.54 ± 6.18 [MCI-to-dementia, N = 28] 5.73 ± 5.46 [MCI-to-MCI, N = 293] 0.032 0.859 / To our surprise, we did not find depressive symptoms markers as predictors of MCI transition to dementia.
supporters.note: Li et al. 2024, J Affect Disord; Shanghai Brain Health Cohort; 1,014 untreated community MCI patients, 321 reached at five years, 28 converters. Supports the conversion half of the severity clause (a baseline GDS score did not separate converters from non-converters). Limits: GDS scale only, no clinical diagnosis of depression and no brain measures; follow-up reached 321 of 1,014 and the authors call this attrition the biggest limitation; the variables entered into the Cox model are not reported, so it is unclear whether GDS was tested in it or only in the univariate Table 4; the cross-sectional GDS correlations with BDT and ADL are weak (r = -0.131 and 0.131). All participants have MCI, so the paper does not test whether depression status is associated with MCI.

supporters.quote: (Table 1) HAMA 7.19 ± 4.03 [controls] 7.87 ± 3.99 [MCI] 0.42 / HAMD 5.26 ± 3.76 5.28 ± 3.31 0.97. (Exclusion criteria) 4) definite history of mental illness such as schizophrenia, major depressive disorder; [...] 10) HAMD ≥14; 11) HAMA ≥21. Searched for any analysis relating HAMD or HAMA to an ERP, source-localisation or behavioural measure: none. The only correlations reported are between the arousal-rating difference and cognitive tests or the late LPP difference (Table 3), plus MMSE (Section 2.6.3).
supporters.note: Xiao et al. 2022, Behav Brain Res; Shanghai Tongji Hospital; 46 amnestic MCI patients and 47 healthy controls (N = 93); 64-channel ERP cognitive-reappraisal task; cross-sectional. The paper never relates depression severity to any brain measure or outcome, so it cannot show that severity scores fail to track them. The equal HAMD scores in patients and controls follow from excluding anyone with a history of MDD or a HAMD score of 14 or more; they are a sample characteristic produced by the exclusions, not a finding about severity grading MCI neurobiology. Read as a finding, equal depression scores in the MCI and control groups would work against the row's first clause rather than for it.

supporters.quote: Searched the full text for any depression scale, depression diagnosis or depression-severity analysis: none. Exclusion criteria included [...] concomitant or recent history of mental illness (p. 2). Personal Distress (PD) measures general anxiety and emotional response to uncomfortable situations (p. 2). The multiple regression model significantly predicted PD-T1 scores (F [3,51] = 10.36, p < 0.001, adj. R2 =0.379). Among the covariates, diagnosis (B=−3.785 [95% CI −7.060:−0.511], p = 0.024) [...] were statistically significant (p. 6).
supporters.note: Giacomucci et al. 2022, Behav Brain Res; Florence; 24 SCD, 41 MCI and 46 AD patients (N = 111); informant-rated Interpersonal Reactivity Index and FDG-PET. The document is the study the ledger describes, but it is about empathy. The Personal Distress subscale measures emotional contagion (anxiety-like distress), not depression severity, and people with mental illness were excluded. The negative coefficient on diagnosis in the Personal Distress model concerns emotional contagion, not depression. The paper cannot support any clause of VF-27.

reasoning: Only two of the four supporters report a result of the kind the Table A1 row describes. P-643 found no correlation between K-GDS severity and ROI volumes or resting-state FC in any of four depressed-MCI subgroups, while its major-depression groups had lower FC than its subthreshold groups (the row's 'although' clause). P-647 found that baseline GDS was the same in converters and non-converters (5.54 versus 5.73, p = 0.859) and that only MoCA predicted five-year conversion. P-662 never relates HAMD or HAMA to any electrophysiological, source or behavioural measure; its equal HAMD scores in patients and controls come from excluding anyone with an MDD history or a HAMD score of 14 or more. P-663 is an empathy study with no depression measure. Two supporters, from two datasets (Korea University Guro; Shanghai Brain Health Cohort) and two method families (imaging correlation; cohort survival analysis), fall short of the three the convergence needs. Neither of the two tests the row's first clause (depression status is associated with MCI): P-643 has no non-depressed MCI group and P-647 enrolled only MCI patients. Both nulls are low-powered: P-643's subgroups have 14 to 28 people with Bonferroni thresholds of 0.002 to 0.006, and P-647 has 28 converters among the 321 of 1,014 it followed up. The ledger note on P-643 also overstates one point: the STD-MCI-A(+) group showed greater FC reduction than the MDD-MCI-A(-) and STD-MCI-A(-) groups, not than the MDD-MCI-A(+) group. What the evidence supports is a two-study observation, not a convergence: in two studies, a continuous depression-severity score did not track structural or functional brain measures (P-643) or five-year conversion (P-647), and in P-643 the major-depression groups nonetheless had lower functional connectivity than the subthreshold groups. P-26 (Ding et al. 2025), which the row cites as outside the supporter list, was not among the documents supplied and was not checked.
